fact: Launched 7 October 2024 (Falcon 9); Mars swingby 12 March 2025 at about 5,000 km altitude, also imaging Deimos.

ESA trajectory design: impulsive rendezvous with Didymos on 12 October 2026, then a two-month rendezvous phase of braking manoeuvres; DSM-2 in February 2026. Hera needs a wider orbit (farther aphelion) than Didymos to phase with it.
quote: Didymos rendezvous phase (RDV) lasts two months

sources.t: Muñoz, Acedo & Khan, Hera Trajectory Design (ISSFD 2024)

fact: Hera is on track to arrive at Didymos in November 2026, a month earlier than planned; farthest point from the Sun in late November 2025.
quote: Hera is on track to arrive at Didymos in November 2026 – a month earlier than originally planned.

sources.t: ESA: Hera targets early arrival at Didymos asteroids (7 Oct 2025)

fact: No public figure found for Hera's farthest distance from the Sun (late November 2025); data.json uses an estimate of 2.4 AU (wider than Didymos's 2.27 AU aphelion).

DART struck Dimorphos on 26 September 2022; Didymos's closest approach to Earth was 4 October 2022 at about 0.071 AU.
